examples: `new Chart` stores eight values and calls nothing; a program starts a chart with `Chart::column` or another type, and the examples of those methods and of `series` and `combine` show every way a chart is built.
perf: `new Chart` stores eight values and calls nothing; every type method, `series` and `combine` build one on every call, so their figures include this one.
hostile: `new Chart` stores eight typed read-only values and calls nothing, so a wrong value does not compile; the titles, ranges, names and colors a request sends are checked when `Sheet::chart` places the chart, and the attacks of the type methods, `series` and `combine` send hostile ones.
